audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] and early both name "Piercing Arrow" as Akshan's poke ability.
audit.why: Piercing Arrow is Varus's Q. Akshan's Q is Avengerang — a boomerang that damages going out and coming back and extends its range each time it hits. This is an ability belonging to a different champion entirely, not a near-miss spelling.
audit.corrected: Avengerang, 9s at rank 1, damaging on both the outbound and return pass.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and whys[4] attribute Akshan's level-6 power spike to Heroic Swing, and mid says "at level 6 he gets global roam".
audit.why: Heroic Swing is his E and is available from level 3, not 6. The roam tool is Going Rogue (W), also available well before 6. What actually arrives at 6 is Comeuppance — a 2500-range lock-on that stores bullets and deals damage scaled to the target's MISSING health. Labelling the wrong ability as the level-6 spike means the reader respects the wrong thing at the wrong time.
audit.corrected: Comeuppance is the level-6 arrival: 100s at rank 1, missing-health scaling, so it is a finisher on a target you are already low against — not a lane-opening threat.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json (E cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12; W range 5500; R: Comeuppance cd 100/85/70, range 2500, "damage based on missing health")

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Comeuppance is stopped by the first body in its path.
audit.why: Riot's own text: the stored bullets deal damage "to the first champion, minion, or structure hit". A single minion between you and Akshan eats the entire ultimate. For a champion with Tahm Kench's movement speed this is the most reliable counter he has to Akshan's only real burst window, and it was completely absent.
audit.corrected: Keep a minion in the line when Comeuppance is charging — it absorbs the whole shot.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json (R: "dealing damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit")

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] tells you to "bait his Heroic Swing grapple anchor into a wall or dead zone", but never mentions that you can end the swing with your own body.
audit.why: Heroic Swing states he "gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain". Standing in the swing arc ends it early. That is a far more reliable answer than trying to bait anchor placement, and it is a free interaction for a 6000-HP frontliner.
audit.corrected: Stand in the swing path — champion collision knocks him off it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json (E: "he can jump off early or gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], whys[2], whys[3], early, tradeGood, breakdown.trading and dosFull all run the "stun into Devour" pattern; whys[3] additionally says "slow with Q, stack, stun, Devour, repeat".
audit.why: The Q stun at 3 stacks consumes all three stacks and Devour requires 3 stacks, so the sequence cannot be executed. "Repeat" compounds the error — Devour is 120s at rank 1, so it is one commitment per fight, not a lane loop.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the stun or the eat. Against Akshan spend them on the eat, and treat it as a 120s resource.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — Devour cooldown 120/100/80, requires and consumes 3 stacks

audit.whatIsWrong: mid describes "a grounded Akshan without Heroic Swing".
audit.why: Grounded is a defined status effect in League and Akshan is not grounded in this scenario — he is simply out of wall range. The file uses "grounded" correctly elsewhere (Cassiopeia's Miasma), so using it loosely here will read as a real status interaction that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Reworded to describe him being denied an anchor, and replaced with the collision interaction that actually applies.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Heroic Swing as matchup-defining and describes it as a "camera swing escape" with no numbers.
audit.why: The reader cannot size a window without a duration. Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1, Avengerang 9s, Comeuppance 100s, Devour 120s.
audit.corrected: Real numbers inserted, plus the two interactions that actually shorten those windows (body collision on E, minion block on R).
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json (E cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12; Q cd 9/8/7/6/5; R cd 100/85/70)

audit.whatIsWrong: Akshan's passive shield is never mentioned.
audit.why: Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit on a champion, and his attacks fire a bonus shot, so the third hit arrives quickly. That shield lands squarely on top of the burst window you are trying to open with your stacks.
audit.corrected: No edit proposed — I could not fit this without displacing a higher-value correction inside the length band, and I will not pad a string to make room. Recorded here so it is not lost.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json (P: "Every three hits... grants him a Shield if the target was a champion")

edits.after: Three stacks buys one payoff — the Q stun or Devour, never both. Spend them on the eat; Akshan has no answer once it lands.

edits.before: Akshan wants to establish Heroic Swing anchor points on jungle-side terrain and kite your Tongue Lash, but at level 1 he has none of that mobility yet — walk up, slow him off each CS with Q, and let An Acquired Taste stacks build naturally. He cannot trade into you at 3 stacks without eating the stun. At level 2-3 your trade pattern is simple: Q to slow, walk through him to auto stack, then the third-stack Q stuns him in place and you follow with Devour — he is gone from the fight and takes bonus damage inside. His Piercing Arrow poke during this window is meaningful but Thick Skin is converting every hit to grey health, so as long as you idle even briefly between exchanges you are healing it back.
edits.after: Akshan wants to establish Heroic Swing anchor points on jungle-side terrain and kite your Tongue Lash, but at level 1 he has none of that mobility yet — walk up, slow him off each CS with Q, and let An Acquired Taste stacks build naturally. He cannot trade into you at 3 stacks without conceding one of them. At level 2-3 your trade pattern is simple: Q to slow, walk through him to auto stack, then choose — the third-stack Q stuns him in place, or you hold the three and Devour instead. His Avengerang poke during this window is meaningful but Thick Skin is converting every hit to grey health, so as long as you idle even briefly between exchanges you are healing it back.

edits.before: Level 4-5 is where you reclaim control: your Q cooldown is comfortable, your grey health pool is growing with each trade, and Akshan does not have the sustained damage to punish you through Thick Skin's passive conversion if you respect his grapple path. Deny him anchor points by standing between him and jungle walls — a grounded Akshan without Heroic Swing is just an auto-attacking ranged champion you can walk down at 3 stacks. At level 6 he gets global roam and can reset kills with his passive revive, which is his only real comeback mechanic in this lane; match his recall timing, ping your team, and do not let him snowball side lanes while you shove.
edits.after: Level 4-5 is where you reclaim control: your Q cooldown is comfortable, your grey health pool is growing with each trade, and Akshan does not have the sustained damage to punish you through Thick Skin's passive conversion if you respect his grapple path. Deny him anchor points by standing between him and jungle walls — and if he swings anyway your body ends it, because colliding with a champion knocks him off Heroic Swing. At 6 Comeuppance adds a 2500-range finisher on anyone already chunked, and his passive revive is his real comeback mechanic; match his recall timing and do not let him snowball side lanes while you shove.

notes:
"Piercing Arrow" in wants.foe[1] and early is not a misspelling — it is Varus's Q attributed to Akshan. Worth checking whether the same wrong-champion substitution appears in other Akshan entries across the site, since it is a different class of error from the near-miss names the packet's suspectNames flags.

The two genuinely decisive interactions in this lane were both missing and both come straight from Riot's ability text: Heroic Swing ends when he collides with a champion (so Tahm Kench's body is the counter, not clever anchor-baiting), and Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure in line (so a single minion eats the whole ultimate). I added both.

Akshan's Dirty Fighting shield is still unmentioned anywhere in the entry — I recorded it in the audit but did not force an edit, because every string long enough to hold it was already carrying a higher-value correction and padding to make room would have pushed other edits out of the length band.
